---
title: "Comparing ME inequalities across groups"
subtitle: "Example 4.3.a of Mize and Han (2025), in R: models fit on different samples"
---

When the question is about different groups or time periods, the comparison
uses a different sample for each. Here the question is whether
religious-tradition differences in willingness to let a gay man speak in
public were larger before 1980 than after 2010. The same example in Stata is
on the [`meinequality` page](/software/meinequality/examples/across-groups.qmd).

## Load and prepare the data

::: {.r-run}
```r
library(haven)           # Read Stata data
library(marginaleffects) # Marginal effects and hypotheses

gss <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss.dta")

vars <- c("spkhomo", "reltrad", "age", "woman", "year")
gss <- gss[complete.cases(gss[vars]), vars]
gss <- gss[gss$year < 1980 | gss$year >= 2010, ]
gss$period <- factor(ifelse(gss$year < 1980, "Before 1980", "2010 and later"),
                     levels = c("Before 1980", "2010 and later"))
gss[c("spkhomo", "reltrad", "woman")] <- lapply(gss[c("spkhomo", "reltrad", "woman")], as_factor)
table(gss$period)
```
```{.r-output}
   Before 1980 2010 and later 
          5593           8226 
```
:::

## Fit the model

Interacting every predictor with `period` is the same as fitting a separate
model to each period, and keeps both in one model for the comparison:

```r
spkmod <- glm(spkhomo ~ (reltrad + age + woman) * period,
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gss)
```

## Unweighted ME inequality in each period

`by = "period"` averages each period's effects over its own sample, and a
small function takes the mean absolute pairwise difference within each period.
`vcov = "HC0"` gives robust standard errors.

::: {.r-run}
```r
meineq <- function(x) {
  est <- sapply(split(x$estimate, x$period), function(e) mean(abs(e)))
  data.frame(term = names(est), estimate = est)
}

ineq <- avg_comparisons(spkmod,
  variables = list(reltrad = "pairwise"),
  by = "period",
  vcov = "HC0",
  hypothesis = meineq)
ineq
```
```{.r-output}
           Term Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)     S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 Before 1980      0.1556    0.01086 14.3   <0.001 152.3 0.1343 0.1768
 2010 and later   0.0722    0.00661 10.9   <0.001  89.7 0.0592 0.0851

Type: response
```
:::

## Test the difference

::: {.r-run}
```r
hypotheses(ineq, hypothesis = difference ~ revpairwise)
```
```{.r-output}
                       Hypothesis Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)    S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 (Before 1980) - (2010 and later)   0.0834     0.0127 6.56   <0.001 34.1 0.0585  0.108
```
:::

The ME inequality is significantly larger before 1980 than after 2010:
religious traditions have converged on this question. The unweighted version
compares the marginal effects alone; the weighted version would also reflect
the change in the religious makeup of the GSS between the two periods.
